new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Searched by food, not by string, across the four namespaces: the only chile-family ids are red-pepper-flakes (dried jar), canned-green-chilies, dried-guajillo-chiles, dried-arbol-chiles, chipotle-adobo and the bell-pepper family. Every one is either dried, canned or a sweet pepper; none prices a fresh hot chile, which is sold loose in produce by the pound. Board reports no commodity and no capture match.

The estate prices sweet-potatoes and baby-potatoes but nothing for plain white/russet potatoes, which are a different food at a different price (bulk 5 lb bags against a bagged creamer SKU and against the sweet variety). Board says no commodity claims it while today's captures carry matching products, the same posture that minted baby-potatoes on 2026-08-26.

registrar_rulings.reason: The mapper's case ('no id prices a fresh hot chile') is false: the live feed prices fresh jalapenos ($1.4277/lb Walmart, loose produce), serrano-peppers ($2.99/lb Family Fare, fresh produce page) and habanero-peppers ($12.64/lb Walmart, fresh tray), none of which the dossier's word-overlap sweep surfaced because they share no token with 'red chili'. A recipe's 'fresh red chilli' is a ripe red jalapeno/fresno-class chile - same species-family, same fresh-loose-by-the-pound purchase, same price class as the green jalapeno the stores actually stock, and the feed already carries a jalapeno->jalapenos alias for exactly this spelling seam. Add fresh-red-chili -> jalapenos to recipe-floor-id-map.json (units match: lb). If a recipe ever genuinely needs the hotter variant, serrano-peppers already exists priced - no new id in any case.

The mapper's claim that nothing prices plain potatoes is contradicted twice over: commodities.json carries russet-potatoes (include patterns for russet/bulk bags), the live feed prices it at $0.409/lb cheapest at Aldi across all 7 stores, and recipe-floor-id-map.json already holds the human-verified pair potato -> russet-potatoes - the exact generic-spelling seam this proposal re-opens. Minting a bare 'potatoes' id beside russet-potatoes, red-potatoes and yukon-gold-potatoes would let the same food price under two ids and its include pattern would inevitably claim the named varieties' products. Add potatoes -> russet-potatoes to recipe-floor-id-map.json (units match: lb) alongside the existing 'potato' pair.
